## [2026-11-14](../../../reports/2026/11/2026-11-14.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [CoReMem: Cost-Internalizing Memory for Successive Coding Tasks with Prospective Valuation](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.17316>)

CoReMem values a completed coding session by how much its contents help the next task on the inherited repository, then compresses useful experience into file locations and executable checks. It also adapts the coding agent to act on those memory anchors, making cross-task memory serve measured task resolution and effort rather than relevance alone. In the reported 27B ChainSWE comparison, the combined memory and training system raises resolution from 21.0% to 25.7% while reducing steps by 17% and session tokens by 11%, without measuring training cost or wall-clock savings.

## [2026-11-13](../../../reports/2026/11/2026-11-13.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Cleaning an Agent's History Hurts When the World Still Holds the Error](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14654>)

By restoring agents to the same intermediate state and independently editing their history or environment, this study tests when correcting a record actually helps recovery. Truthful annotations and falsely completed actions have opposite effects in the tested settings, showing why context repair should preserve the distinction between a claimed action and its verified effect. The interventions offer a useful way to evaluate memory and handoff policies, while differences in wording and message roles prevent isolating truthfulness as the sole cause.

**Published:** 2026-11-10 · **First seen:** 2026-11-13T11:06:28.151+00:00 · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Context Engineering, Error Recovery, Controlled Evaluation

**Public availability:** 2026-11-13T01:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new>) · [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.14654v1>) · [Code](<https://arxiv.org/src/2611.14654v1/anc>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Main pages 1-8 and scientific AppendicesA-K pages 11-23 read; result/limitation pages 6-7 also visually inspected. On 319 AgentCE-Bench frozen states, two receivers and four arms produce 2,552 continuations under 24-step caps. The same verified correct value is appended as an error-preserving note or written into a falsely completed action while the erroneous world stays fixed; the note gains 15.20 percentage points over a role/position/turn/length-matched neutral append, whereas falsification loses 6.43 points versus its padded original record. The primary difference of contrasts is 21.63 points, 95% task-cluster bootstrap interval \[18.21, 25.08\]. AppWorld independently crosses receipt and pre/post database state over 65 task families, two receivers and two repetitions (1,040 continuations); the pooled success-minus-failure receipt effect is -16.92 points with the write absent and +10.38 once present, interaction 27.31 points with 97.5% family-bootstrap interval \[14.23, 41.54\]. Released ancillary directory/README/manifest, primary contrast table and 65-family readout were inspected without execution. Original v1 receipt is November 10 19:06:36UTC; first original AI announcement is the Friday November 13 batch, implying November 13 01:00UTC from the official EST schedule following the November 11 holiday. No earlier public artifact was verified.

**Limitations:** These are author-designed interventions, not an evaluated deployable compaction/repair policy or an estimate of real-world mismatch prevalence. Truth/channel/authorship/error visibility/remaining-work cues differ between the two AgentCE edits; the truthful arm uses an oracle value, and AppWorld success/failure receipts differ in content. Most note gain is local to its named slot,24-step caps bind unevenly, receiver operating points differ, and most runs are cross-model handoffs. AppWorld begins every continuation with a fresh interpreter. Its sealed preregistered estimator did not run; reported estimates come from two agreeing contract reimplementations, with author-side endpoint rescoring/re-execution rather than an independent reproduction. The separate targeted control is incomplete (4,068 of 4,320) with post-hoc frames and a specificity interval that fails its3-point margin. The eight-receiver extension uses unadjusted fixed-model intervals and a post-hoc added GPT-4o; it is not a model-family population guarantee. Ancillary analysis code/readouts are available, but the third-party AgentCE fork is not redistributed.

## [2026-11-13](../../../reports/2026/11/2026-11-13.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Folio: Recoverable Multi-Resolution Context Folding for Long-Horizon Language Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.16627>)

Folio records turn notes, event manifests and captured source records while an agent runs, then folds old context by selecting existing views instead of generating a fresh summary. Stable handles support bounded rereading and file-side analysis of removed evidence, while a cache-priced trigger accounts for how much context the fold will retain. The authors report better success and lower normalized cost than model-written compaction in one matched runtime on 75 tasks, with broader generalization and security left open.

**Published:** 2026-11-12 · **First seen:** 2026-11-13T11:06:28.151+00:00 · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Context Folding, Recoverable Memory, Prompt Caching

**Public availability:** 2026-11-13T01:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new>) · [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/pdf/2611.16627v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. All 13 PDF pages read; setup/results/ablation tables on pages 7-9 visually inspected. L1 notes are model-written during ordinary replies; L2 manifests and L3 captured records are runtime-written, sharing call handles with byte-offset/digest lookup and fallback parsing. Monotone demotion preserves already sent prefix text; scan,ctx and a persistent dossier recover/use captured evidence. The trigger accumulates cached input above S=B+L+D against rewrite cost rho\_w(L+D), with a separate window safety line; the reference uses L = 50K and DeepSeek-V4-Pro ratios 1:30:90. Five 15-task LOCA-bench sessions run once per system, all on DeepSeek-V4-Pro: Folio1M solves 66/75 versus 54/75 for the same Piki runtime with model-written compaction, discordant 14:2 exact McNemar p = .004. Mean cached-read-equivalent cost is 19.75M versus 47.00M tokens/task (2.38x ratio, including summary/retry usage), and working time 10.2 versus 16.3 minutes/task, excluding setup/grading. The main 85 folds have a median of 613 ms and no re-render mismatch. Original v1 receipt November 12 10:59:40UTC and original Friday November 13 AI batch support inferred November 13 01:00UTC availability. No author implementation/project or earlier public artifact was verified.

**Limitations:** One model, one benchmark/price structure, five chains each run once; chain-order dependencies and deterministic graders constrain inference. The benchmark contamination scan flags 8 Folio and 11 Piki-Classic runs and keeps them in reported totals. Score gaps from Claude Code(p = .19) and Codex(p = .06) do not resolve at .05; their provider usage is unavailable, so no cross-harness cost comparison is established. Removing dossier/L1 changes too little to distinguish from chain variation; deeper cumulative ablations cover one chain and the recovery-removal run has 21 provider retries plus 3 timeout/agent-error failures. Of 809 folds across all reported runs, one mismatch occurred in a discarded infrastructure-error variant run. Recoverability covers only captured, still-stored records with valid handles, and cut/missing/oversized source files are disclosed; model notes can be wrong. The trigger omits unknown future recovery/reasoning costs from its immediate threshold, though later billed requests count them. ctx isolation/permissions are inherited from the runtime and unevaluated; no general safety, universal savings or independent reproduction is claimed.

## [2026-11-11](../../../reports/2026/11/2026-11-11.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Don't Just Trust Your Memory: Evidence-Linked Memory Reduces Memory-Induced Degradation in LLM Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14320>)

WikiTrace links each reusable lesson to a diagnostic summary and its unchanged source trajectory, allowing an agent to inspect the evidence before applying questionable advice. Across the authors’ eight configured suites, this improves average performance by 3.2 points over the same insights alone and reduces memory-induced regression from 6.5% to 4.5%, at 17% higher average test-time cost. It provides a practical pattern for auditable experience reuse, while leaving very large memory retrieval and automatic verification of lessons unresolved.

Anthropic evaluates a layered memory design in which agents keep transcripts and notes, then use offline consolidation to correct errors, build linked knowledge wikis and choose what future sessions receive. The engineering report shows where maintained representations can complement search, while emphasizing that stale notes, concurrent writes and consolidation cost require explicit design choices.

On 25 questions over a private 420M-token corpus, search alone scores 53% of criteria versus 61% with the mature wiki plus search; wiki-only reaches 48%. Building scales from two to 128 sessions. ### [Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.06500>)

CocaCola compresses a tool observation into task- and reasoning-conditioned latent vectors, training the compressor to preserve a frozen agent’s next-action behavior rather than reconstruct the original text. This can shrink the agent’s context while retaining useful retrieval evidence, provided the deployment supports direct embedding inputs.

### [CALM: Conflict-Aware Lifecycle Memory Governance for Long-Horizon Language Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.38573>)

CALM preserves superseded memories for historical questions while controlling which records enter an agent’s current reasoning context. Deterministic lifecycle rules track conflicts and dependencies, and a separate fixed or learned gate admits evidence according to the query, helping avoid stale but semantically relevant context.

### [Cache Engineering for Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28577>)

Cache engineering lets an agent drop selected KV states and reposition retained keys without rewriting its text history; AKV tracks operation history so shared or restored caches remain consistent. The full-paper study reports 1.7 points higher average task scores and 27.7% lower estimated token cost than threshold summarization across three models and four agent benchmarks, suggesting a useful route to context control when builders also control the serving engine.

**Published:** 2026-10-20 · **First seen:** 2026-10-21T10:02:45.248Z · **Novelty:** material-update · **Tags:** Context Engineering, KV Cache, Serving

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.28577>) · [Code](<https://github.com/thu-nics/AKV>) · [Project](<https://fuvty.github.io/thinking_yard_project_page/projects/akv/>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Full Sections 3–5, Tables 1–4 and Appendices A.1–A.4 inspected. Drop changes future attention but not retained hidden states; repos rotates retained RoPE keys and resets future position indices, rather than making them equivalent to recomputing a shortened text. AKV uses operation-aware radix branches, drop-aware eviction and segmented restoration. Main policy retains the latest 12 tool responses plus reasoning, with model-specific position thresholds. Three-model/four-benchmark tests report mean 1.7 score-point gain and 27.7% API-equivalent agent/summary token-cost reduction versus Standard; costs exclude other tools and are not billed GPU expenditure. Eight A800-80GB BF16 GPT-OSS-120B serving replay reports 1.18 times output throughput and 1.51 times P95 request-latency speedup at each method's own peak concurrency. Original cs.CL October 21 batch plus official announcement schedule supports inferred formal-study availability2026-10-21T00:00Z. The September 28 repository and pinned October 15 README already document the drop/repos implementation but contain no benchmark results; this is proposed as the new full-paper evaluation/formalization over an older code preview, not as a newly invented operation.

**Limitations:** Cached hidden states retain information from previously attended dropped tokens, and arbitrary policies can degrade quality; serving support for linear-attention models remains future work. Serving replay selects 80 longest-context SWE tasks and replays recorded tool outputs with method-specific trajectories/budgets, not identical live workloads. API-equivalent prices and reposition charges are modeling assumptions. The current results-bearing project page is accessible, but its source repository/history returns 404, so earlier project-page visibility cannot be reconstructed and exact global first public visibility is uncertain. No independent reproduction.

**Update:** 2026-10-21: The first arXiv paper adds a formal operation-history account and a three-model/four-benchmark evaluation to the older AKV implementation preview. The verified October 15 README already describes drop/repos and compatible-cache reuse, so those mechanisms are not claimed as new on this date; exact earlier project-page visibility is unresolved.

Hippocam organizes ongoing work into nested intents, compressing completed work and older history while preserving original messages in a recallable tree. Recalled experience is consolidated again with new outcomes, allowing useful details and lessons to evolve without changing model weights.

**Published:** 2026-10-08 · **First seen:** 2026-10-09T10:05:20Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Agent Memory, Context Consolidation, Progressive Recall

**Public availability:** 2026-10-09T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/new>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.12124>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Sections 2–5 and Appendix A describe the memory operations and ablations. With the same 64K MemoryAgentBench snapshot, recall achieves 41% accuracy versus 27% when disabled across 100 questions. Original v1: 2026-10-08T15:16:56Z; October 9 new-submission batch.

**Limitations:** Single runs and unmatched auxiliary compute limit system comparisons; interfaces and reasoning settings differ across baselines. LoCoMo uses an LLM judge rather than its original lexical score. Reported cost advantages depend on caching prices and workload. No author code artifact was verified.

## [2026-10-08](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-08.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [RunningTab: Direct Workspace Interaction with Environment-Side Tabs](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.10444>)

RunningTab maintains an external ledger of task requirements, captured file-reading observations and unopened candidate files while an agent works directly in a workspace. Requirement-focused review and a final completion check help the agent recover evidence that has left its context and identify missing parts of a deliverable.

**Published:** 2026-10-07 · **First seen:** 2026-10-08T10:03:51Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Working Memory, Evidence Tracking, Workspace Agents

**Public availability:** 2026-10-08T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.AI/recent>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.10444v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Across three models and three workspace benchmarks, the authors report consistent gains over direct interaction and model-managed tracking. For DeepSeek V4 Flash, Workspace-Bench rubric pass rate rises from 53.28% to 59.99%, averaged over three runs; component ablations support the design. All methods share a 300-turn and one-hour task limit.

**Limitations:** The citation gate checks lexical overlap, not semantic correctness. Two benchmarks use restricted subsets, and the capture ablation also removes dependent review/evidence features. Equal turn limits do not establish equal cost; no public implementation link was located.

## [2026-10-06](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-06.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [MemPilot: Orchestrating On-Demand Multimodal Memory Curation for LLM Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06830>)

MemPilot learns when to reuse compressed memory and when to ask another model to re-examine raw text or images for the current question. Jointly choosing evidence volume, processing instructions and model capacity provides a way to balance answer quality against memory-processing cost and modeled latency.

**Published:** 2026-10-05 · **First seen:** 2026-10-06T10:03:31Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Multimodal Memory, Adaptive Retrieval, Resource-Aware Policies

**Public availability:** 2026-10-06T00:00:00Z (inferred from dated announcement and official schedule). [Timing source](<https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/recent?skip=0&show=2000>) · [Timing source](<https://info.arxiv.org/help/availability.html>)

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.06830v1>) · [Code](<https://github.com/ViktorAxelsen/MemPilot>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. The authors evaluate five memory benchmarks, including two held-out distributions, with separate downstream answer models and ablations of routing and reward credit. Reinforcement learning trains policies with different quality, monetary-cost and latency preferences; implementation and configuration files are publicly accessible.

**Limitations:** Reported latency uses a token-based proxy rather than measured deployment wall time, and cost aggregates questions per conversation history rather than per question. Filtered benchmark splits, model-based grading and one greedy trajectory per query constrain comparisons. Preference changes are evaluated through trained policies; the paper does not establish universal gains or a free runtime adjustment.

## [2026-10-03](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-03.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02163>)

AutoCompact trains a coding agent to decide when to summarize its history, preserve a useful working state, and continue consistently from that summary. Judge-corrected demonstrations followed by task-success reinforcement learning improve repository problem solving even when the original history fits in the context window.

**Published:** 2026-10-01 · **First seen:** 2026-10-03T10:03:03Z · **Novelty:** newly-discovered · **Tags:** Context Compaction, Coding Agents, Reinforcement Learning

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.02163v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Three-run evaluations use one Qwen3-Coder backbone and a shared scaffold on SWE-bench Verified and SWE-PolyBench Verified, reporting 9.2 and 5.0 percentage-point gains over the base agent. Disabling compaction in the same trained checkpoint reduces performance, supporting a contribution beyond weight updates. Newly discovered in this run; its Oct 2 public announcement precedes the main window but falls within the 72-hour lookback.

**Limitations:** Evidence covers one model and coding tasks. Inference costs are token-price estimates excluding training and judge-guided data collection; summary-quality checks use keyword screening with manual spot checks. No code or checkpoint link was found in the inspected primary publication, and results were not independently reproduced.

## [2026-10-02](../../../reports/2026/10/2026-10-02.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Causal Memory Policy: Making Memory Utility Identifiable by Intervening on Retrieval](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.02070>)

Causal Memory Policy randomizes a few retrieval slots so memories that the normal retriever misses can still have their effect on a specific answer measured. This provides a diagnostic for biased memory-utility estimates, while showing that accurate per-query measurements alone do not tell an agent what to retain for future questions.

**Published:** 2026-10-01 · **First seen:** 2026-10-02T15:33:55Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** Memory, Causal Evaluation, Retrieval

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2610.02070v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Inspected the intervention design, estimator assumptions, benchmark comparisons and explicit limitations. LongMemEval experiments improve required-memory discrimination from 0.542 to 0.664 AUC, with additional analyses on LoCoMo, multi-hop QA and Mem0.

**Limitations:** The main identification demonstration uses a candidate pool constructed with knowledge of required memories; tested deployable selectors fail to recover that pool reliably. Exposure consumes context and the work makes no effective retention-policy claim. The linked anonymous code page yielded no readable content; not independently reproduced.

## [2026-09-30](../../../reports/2026/09/2026-09-30.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [ContextRender: From Execution Dependencies to Agent Context](<https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.37743>)

ContextRender keeps complete tool results in a persistent graph and selects what the agent sees using observed value reuse, recency, and relevance. This gives long-running agents a way to reduce repeated context costs while retaining omitted information for later recovery, with competitive task performance under a 6K history budget.

**Published:** 2026-09-29 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T10:01:45Z · **Novelty:** new · **Tags:** context-management, tool-use, long-horizon

[Paper](<https://arxiv.org/html/2609.37743v1>)

**Evidence:** research-paper; full-text. Full methods, matched-budget baselines and ablations inspected; three models on AppWorld and 8-objective QA. Reports better task performance than five managed-context baselines across nine settings and 10.2–32.2% lower standardized inference cost than full history. The arXiv v1 submission was 2026-09-29T14:57:00Z, within the daily interval.

**Limitations:** Costs use a common pricing/cache model and only tasks triggering context management; they are not measured provider-bill savings. Performance is below full history in two settings. Reuse detection is exact, case-sensitive value matching; no independent reproduction or verified code release.

## [2026-09-29 — Landscape baseline](../../../landscape/2026-09-29.md) — PARTIAL SEARCH

### [Effective context engineering for AI agents](<https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents>)

Anthropic describes a context-management approach that combines selective retrieval, conversation compaction, persistent notes, and separate subagent contexts. These patterns help long-running agents retain decisions and recover relevant information without carrying every prior observation in the active prompt.

**Published:** 2025-09-29 · **First seen:** 2026-09-30T04:13:56.564Z · **Novelty:** baseline · **Tags:** Context Engineering, Memory, Long-Horizon

**Positioning:** established-method

[Blog](<https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents>)

**Evidence:** engineering-report; full-text. The dated September 29, 2025 engineering article explains concrete implementations in Claude Code, including retrieving by lightweight references and preserving unresolved work during compaction. It is selected as an implementation reference for working context and memory.

**Limitations:** This is engineering guidance with product examples, not a controlled comparison establishing the best memory algorithm. Compression can discard critical details, and runtime retrieval adds latency.
